verdict: The proposal's diagnosis is CORRECT and reproduced on real structures: a rigid Lennard-Jones evaluation hits the r^-12 wall and returns impossible energies for bulky interface mutations (demo ->Trp cases read 1e6-1e10 kcal/mol). But testing the FIX against measured SKEMPI gives a more honest, more useful answer than the proposal assumed: local backbone MINIMISATION alone is necessary but NOT sufficient — it relieves MODERATE clashes (e.g. 1JCK B20->Trp 1334 -> 178) yet cannot rescue a deeply BURIED bulky clash by moving atoms alone (a fixed-rotamer Trp jammed in an Ile pocket stays explosive), because full relief also needs ROTAMER sampling, which position-only gradient descent doesn't do. The robust practical fix is the SOFT-CORE (capped repulsion) I added: it returns physical values for 92% of mutations vs 67% for rigid, and on the larger-residue set it is the best-correlated clash score (soft-core Spearman +0.35 vs rigid +0.35, flex +0.38). The REAL win, though, is patching physics into the research: the WT sidechain's buried cross-interface contact count alone tracks measured alanine ΔΔG at r~0.47, and adding physics to the interface-research features lifts complex-held-out r from 0.37 to 0.48 (+0.12) — real structural burial beats coarse position labels. HONEST LIMITS: a REDUCED force field (vdW + soft-core + harmonic restraints, uniform eps, single fixed-rotamer mutant, no rotamer packing / electrostatics / solvation), so absolute ΔΔG is a TRIAGE signal not FoldX/Rosetta accuracy; and it speaks only to the near-field INTERFACE effect, not the downstream cellular consequence. Net: your steric-clash fix is real, the soft-core is the practical form of it, and the biggest gain came from feeding real interface geometry into the empirical predictor.
